public/js/app-view.js.why: Made-up sample apps for the ?shot= screenshot fixtures (showLaunchShot, showAppToneShot, showOfflineShot, showFirstVersionShot): their names and description, the sample plan, build caption and maker's note, and the labels drawn into the sample pictures (_firstVersionSampleScreen). They stand in for an app's own data, not interface text. _proposalsCtx.lockedHint is an HTML fragment that nothing reads any more; dead data, left untouched. ArrowDown, ArrowUp, Home and End are keyboard key names compared with event.key. Claude Code and Codex are product names (EXTERNAL_AGENT_NAMES), passed to messages as {{agent}}. The last two are error replies to an embedded app that only its developer can cause (a file save with no bytes, lookupUser called without a username). 'desktop' is the default viewport key of a shots claim, looked up and mapped to a size word by _shotsSizeWord. 'you' is a key that picks a message id in _workStateNote ('you' | 'named' | 'someone').

frontend/src/features/dev-chat/dev-chat..why: Product, venue and model names. They are passed to messages as {{venue}}, {{agent}}, {{product}} and never translated. DevChat.MODELS default table: a copy of the server's /api/models answer (label and changeSize), replaced wholesale by loadModels(). Server-worded data; the 'short' hints beside them are the same. System-row `content` in the server's own vocabulary: the server persists the same sentences (src/routes/sessions.js) and the client's live echo must equal the reloaded row; code also keys off them. stagingErrorName 'Error' is an error class name. Fixtures for ?shot= / demo states: they stand in for server sentences and for text a person typed. Key suffixes that pick an id from _OPENROUTER_TITLE_IDS, not text. Quick-reply pills (STARTER_QUICK_REPLIES, _starterQuickReplies and FALLBACK_QUICK_REPLIES): the server holds the same literals (RECOVERY_PILLS / BANNED_GENERIC_PILLS in src/services/recovery-pills.js, pinned equal by tests/quick-reply-fallback.test.js) and compares against them, and a pressed pill is sent as the person's message. They need a server-side decision before they can be worded per language. 'included' is a key into the _OPENROUTER_TITLE_IDS table of message ids, never shown.
